doc: Row selection per compute capability: `order` = preference among the rows that can serve a call (envelopes in `rows`); `measured` = the per-shape evidence behind the order (ms per call, same process, interleaved arms; see the notes shipped with the release). A call no row serves is refused by name with `fallback`.

cuda_sm90a.why: k2b_aot measured faster below S 384 on cc 9.0 (S 256: 0.21-0.26 vs 0.22-0.29 ms; S 448: 0.57 vs 0.51 ms)

triattn_native.why: policy for this kernel family (fastest measured row wins; a TIE goes to the family's own generation-11 kernel): auto takes triattn_native from S 500 in every mask form on cc 9.0 (bf16, head_dim 32). Evidence: triattn_native WINS beyond noise at key-mask S >= 1280 (pad 3 %: x1.05-1.13 at 1280-3584, x1.04 at 4096; 8 %: x1.10-1.18; 14 %: x1.17-1.33, both jax lines) and at no-mask S 2048-2559 (-7.4 / -6.8 %); it TIES cuda_sm90a everywhere else from S 500 (no mask 512 +1.9/-0.2/+1.0 %, 768 -5.3/-2.8/-2.6 %, 1216 +0.8/+1.4/+1.7 %, 1536 -2.0..-7.1 %, 2560-4096 -0.7..-3.5 %; key padding 768 +9.5/-2.1/-2.6 %, 1024 -4.2/+3.9 %, 1216 -2.6/-2.4/+3.7 % -- jax 0.10.2 / 0.6.0 / 0.5.3 lines; a one-line +9.5 % against two lines at -2 % is a tie by the same >= 5 %-beyond-noise-on-both-lines standard a win needs); below S 500 triattn_native LOSES (+2..+19 % at S <= 448: its routed band starts at 512 and an adopting design program measured its own floor at 500 tokens by word) -> cuda_sm90a serves 384 <= S < 500 and k2b_aot below 384 (rules.cuda_sm90a). The lower edge 500 (not 512) is that program's measured floor (source: its former per-row floor table, native 500 / sm90a 384 / bridge from 384 tokens); the S 512 cells here tie.

history.note: before the tie policy auto took triattn_native only where it won beyond noise (no mask [2048, 2560); key mask >= 1280 since 1.6.0)

triattn_native.in_model: an AlphaFold-3 JAX program on H100 (its pairformer, bf16, per program): triattn_native vs cuda_sm90a 0.00 / -0.05 / -0.58 / -2.24 % at S 448 / 832 / 1216 / 2048; per call -5.4 / -6.9 % at 2048, -1.3 / -3.2 % at 3072 (that program's own measurement)

forms.design_model_bf16_h4_d32_keymask: an adopting design program's call form (bf16, 4 heads, head_dim 32, key padding, S = binder + target tokens): below 384 tokens the program keeps its own attention path (its gate, source: its former table); 384 <= S < 500 -> cuda_sm90a; S >= 500 -> triattn_native -- exactly what auto serves under the rules above, so the program binds auto and deletes its floor table
forms.structure_model_bf16_h4_d32_pad: the AF3-family pairformer form (bf16, 4 heads, head_dim 32, key padding to the bucket): auto = k2b_aot below 384, cuda_sm90a 384-499, triattn_native from 500

8.0.rows_doc: cuda_80 = the kernel family's sm_80 member (bf16, head_dim 16/32/64, any key mask); k2b_aot = the sm_80 Triton cubins (bf16 + fp32/TF32). auto takes cuda_80 where the cc 8.0 cells below show it >= 5 % faster than k2b_aot outside both arms' IQR boxes on BOTH jax reference lines (0.10.2 and 0.5.3, A100-SXM4-80GB), per (head_dim, mask form, S): rules.cuda_80; elsewhere k2b_aot keeps (parity = incumbent), cuda_80 selectable by word; fp32 calls: k2b_aot (cuda_80 is bf16 only, refused by name)

masked.why: key-mask calls: D32 H4 wins from S 400 on both lines (x1.21/1.24 at 400, x1.48-1.70 at 800-2048 over k2b_aot); D16 H4 wins from S 256 (x1.21 / x1.22-1.32 at 256, x1.29-1.36 at 400, x1.66-1.86 at 800-1200); D32 S 256: parity (-3.1 / -2.2 % and +2.3 / -15.1 % with overlapping IQR boxes) -> k2b_aot

cuda_80.why: no-mask calls: D32 H4 wins from S 400 on both lines (x1.10-1.13 / x1.12 at 400 by the 5x9 confirm runs, x1.16-1.32 at 800-2048); D32 S 256 parity (x1.03-1.05 / x0.97-1.15, IQR boxes overlap) -> k2b_aot; D16 no-mask: S 400 wins on the 0.10.2 line (x1.10) but is parity on the 0.5.3 line (-13.1 % with overlapping boxes) -> auto from S 800 (x1.18 / x1.23), S 256 parity; head_dim 64: no JAX program uses it and no cell was measured -> by word only
cuda_80.measured_on: A100-SXM4-80GB, jax 0.10.2 line and jax 0.5.3 line (forward per call, bf16, H 4, rows = S = N, layout BNHSD, arms xla fp32 / xla bf16 / the Pallas kernel / k2b_aot / cuda_80 in one process, 3 warm-ups, 3 interleaved rounds x 5; the S 256 / 400 cells re-timed at 4 warm-ups, 5 rounds x 9)

8.0.lines: line-independent: every cc 8.0 row launches the same shipped bytes on every jax line (cuda_80 = one CUDA library, k2b_aot = the same sm_80 cubins; only the launcher build differs per XLA-FFI header version, not the kernels), so the cells measured on the jax 0.10.2 and 0.5.3 lines (A100-SXM4-80GB) hold for the jax 0.6.0 line and any other line the launcher serves (measured_on: those two lines); the XLA / Pallas comparison arms are line-specific and were raced on both

forms.structure_model_bf16_h4_d32_pad: the AF3-family pairformer form on cc 8.0: auto = cuda_80 from S 400 (x1.21-1.70 over k2b_aot in the key-padding form at 400-2048, both lines), k2b_aot at 256 <= S < 400 (parity cell); an adopting structure program measured k2b_aot vs its fused Pallas attention core at +1.1 % per program at 448 / 832 / 1216 tokens (source: its in-program A/B) -- i.e. parity with the Pallas core -- so with cuda_80 x1.2-1.7 over k2b_aot at those sizes the bridge's auto is the faster core there; below 400 the program's Pallas core / k2b_aot are at parity
forms.design_model_bf16_h4_d32_keymask: the design form on cc 8.0: auto = cuda_80 from S 400, k2b_aot below (same cells); the jax 0.6.0 line inherits (see 'lines')

vjp.doc: the differentiable row (vjp=<word>): forward = k2bl cubins (K2B forward + per-row log-sum-exp; out bit-identical to k2b_aot), backward = by_cc[<cc>][<dtype>] order of backwards (attbwd = kernels/pallas_triatt attbwd_dkdv; flash / flash_xla = kernels/pallas_attn af2_flash_pallas backward with d(bias) summed in-kernel / per-row partials reduced by XLA), first that imports on the running jax; residual memory out + lse = B*N*H*SQ*(D*itemsize + 4) bytes; partial-sum memory: attbwd ceil(N/G)*H*SQ*SKp*itemsize (G = knobs.attbwd.k2.G), flash H*SQ*SK*4, flash_xla N*H*SQ*SK*itemsize; flash_xla is refused (by name) when its partials exceed knobs.flash.dbias_xla_max_bytes, so `auto` in fp32 takes flash_xla below ~N 320 (H 4) and flash above

vjp.by_cc_doc: bf16: attbwd first on every card (fwd+bwd -3..-11 % vs the kit Pallas triatt op at N 500/800, cc 9.0 and 8.0, jax 0.6.0 and 0.10.2). fp32: cc 9.0 flash_xla below the partials cap then flash (attbwd is slower there: 26-32 vs 21-25 ms at N 800); cc 8.x flash first: attbwd is 2.5 % faster under jax 0.10.2 at N 800 but its fp32 tiles exceed the sm_80 shared-memory limit under the jax 0.6.0 line's Triton (173,056 > 166,912 B at N 800), flash runs on both. cc 8.6 / 8.9 inherit 8.0's order unmeasured.
vjp.fwd_doc: cc 9.0: cuda_lse first -- fwd+bwd (bwd attbwd) vs the k2bl forward, bf16, rows = S = N, H 4: N 200 / 500 / 800 = -2.3..-4.0 % / -3.4..-5.9 % / -2.0..-5.0 % (jax 0.6.0 and 0.10.2, mask none and pad); min_S 128 = the kernel's query tile (below it unmeasured; k2bl serves); TRIATTN_XLA_VJP_FWD=<name> forces one

by_cc_doc: 1.4.1: `order` lists the rows impl='auto' tries (first that serves wins, subject to `rules`); `by_word_only` lists rows present in the package that auto never takes on this card (selectable by impl=<row>). A row enters `order` ahead of an incumbent only where the same-process cells show it >= 5 % faster outside the two arms' IQR overlap in the form the engines call; parity keeps the incumbent. | 1.4.2: a rule may carry `max_S_excl` (auto steps past the row from that S up) besides `min_S`; `in_model` quotes an adopting program's own end-to-end numbers beside the per-call cells.
